confirmed.title: render({ target: null }) throws instead of falling back to the canvas as Pixi does
confirmed.description: The branch only treats `target === undefined` (or the renderer's own canvas) as the canvas. Pixi treats any falsy target as the view's render target (`options.target ||= this.view.renderTarget`). With `target: null`, `toCanvas` is false, so `renderStart(null)` → `FrameBuilder.resolveTarget(null)` → `this.ctx.textures.get(null)` → TypeError at GpuTextures.ts:82 (`source.destroyed`). The planner's catch returns the pool textures and rethrows, so the frame is lost. `lastObjectRendered`, the background clear colour and clearBeforeRender are also skipped, where Pixi applies them.
confirmed.reference: node_modules/pixi.js/lib/rendering/renderers/shared/system/AbstractRenderer.mjs:83-88 (`options.target || (options.target = this.view.renderTarget); if (options.target === this.view.renderTarget) { _lastObjectRendered = …; clearColor ??= background.colorRgba; clear ??= background.clearBeforeRender }`)
confirmed.failure_scenario: renderer.render({ container: root, target: null }). Pixi draws root to the canvas with the background clear. engine2d throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'destroyed')`. Repro: tmp/review/r4-gpu-core/nulltarget.test.ts (passes, and records the error in nulltarget.txt).
confirmed.game_impact: None found. Every game call site passes a live RenderTexture: GiBouncePass.ts:251, SceneLightingPass.ts:1633, shadowPrefix.ts:437/449/456, backgroundSway.ts:1112, irradianceProbe.ts:42, BurnRenderer.ts:390-391, PlaceholderFactory.ts:68, WaterMinigameScene.ts:720/727, contactAo.ts:423/434/457. Only a future caller that passes a nullable RT would hit it.
confirmed.suggested_fix: `const toCanvas = !options.target || options.target === this.canvas;` (keep the `this.canvas` identity so the existing behaviour is unchanged).

primary.reasoning:
Branch src/engine2d/gpu/WebGPURenderer.ts:201 computes `toCanvas = options.target === undefined || options.target === this.canvas`, so `target: null` is treated as an offscreen surface: builder.renderStart(null) goes into resolveTarget / textures.get(null) and throws a TypeError. Pixi 8.17 (node_modules/pixi.js/lib/rendering/renderers/shared/system/AbstractRenderer.mjs:83-88) does `options.target || (options.target = this.view.renderTarget)`, so any falsy target renders to the canvas and also applies lastObjectRendered, background.colorRgba and clearBeforeRender.

Repro: tmp/review/verify-r4-gpu-core-0/nulltarget.test.ts, run under NullRhiDevice, 2/2 pass. As a control, `target: undefined` renders to the canvas and sets lastObjectRendered. `target: null` throws a TypeError and leaves lastObjectRendered null. A canvas render afterwards still works, so no state is left stuck (the catch/abort path recovers). Pixi could not be run side by side in node because it needs WebGL, but its code is unambiguous.

Game impact: none. Every game call to renderer.render with a target passes a RenderTexture that is null-guarded or non-nullable:
- SceneLightingPass.ts:1633: guarded at :1612
- GiBouncePass.ts:251: guarded at :249
- contactAo.ts:423/434/457: guarded at :399 and :491
- BurnRenderer.ts:390-391: guarded at :384
- WaterMinigameScene.ts:720/727: non-nullable fields
- backgroundSway.ts:1112: readonly uvMap
- shadowPrefix.ts:437/449/456: RenderTexture[] elements
- PlaceholderFactory.ts:68 and irradianceProbe.ts:42: freshly created RTs

Canvas renders go through the Application ticker with no target. So this is an API divergence the game does not hit, and severity is low.
primary.fix_suggestion: In src/engine2d/gpu/WebGPURenderer.ts:201 replace the check with `const toCanvas = !options.target || options.target === this.canvas;`. This matches Pixi's `options.target ||= this.view.renderTarget`, and the existing `toCanvas ? 'canvas' : options.target` branch then handles null. Optionally add a unit test asserting that `render({container, target: null})` sets lastObjectRendered and records a canvas pass.

confirmed.title: Canvas targets with different depth formats in one frame share luma's single canvas depth texture; the second format destroys the first
confirmed.description: `swapchainWithDepth(format)` keeps one LumaSwapchainTarget per depth format (the `swapchainDepth` Map). Each target gets its depth view from `context.getCurrentFramebuffer({depthStencilFormat})` (line 492), and caches that view for the rest of the frame (`passViews`, line 496). luma's WebGPUCanvasContext has only one depth slot. `_createDepthStencilAttachment(format)` destroys the existing depth texture and makes a new one whenever the requested format differs from the stored one. The RHI contract says each format gets its own depth texture, and NullRhiDevice (lines 709-724) does create a separate NullTexture per format. So the Null backend accepts a pattern that the real backend turns into an invalid submit.
confirmed.reference: node_modules/@luma.gl/webgpu/dist/adapter/webgpu-canvas-context.js:_createDepthStencilAttachment (`needsNewDepthStencilAttachment = ... || this.depthStencilAttachment.format !== depthStencilFormat` → `this.depthStencilAttachment?.destroy()`); RhiDevice.ts RhiFrame.swapchainWithDepth doc ('设备持有,尺寸随画布变' per format); NullRhiDevice.ts:709-724
confirmed.failure_scenario: In one runFrame: pass A on frame.swapchainWithDepth('depth24plus'), then pass B on frame.swapchainWithDepth('depth24plus-stencil8'). B's getCurrentFramebuffer destroys A's depth GPUTexture, but pass A (and A's cached view for any later pass) still references it. queue.submit then fails with a 'destroyed texture used in submit' validation error and the whole frame is dropped. Alternating formats reproduces this every frame. NullRhiDevice runs the same sequence without error.
confirmed.game_impact: None today. engine2d only ever asks for STENCIL_DEPTH_FORMAT (WebGPURenderer.ts:343, FrameBuilder pushDraw), so there is only one canvas depth format. This is an API hazard and a Null/luma parity gap, not a game path. The bug predates the 2855653 view-caching change.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Let the RHI own the canvas depth textures per format (like LumaMsaaSwapchainTarget does with depthTex), or reject a second distinct canvas depth format in a frame with RhiError in both backends.

primary.reasoning:
I reproduced this in node with .claude/review-repros/engine2d-r4/verify-r4-rhi-0/canvasDepthFormats.test.ts; both tests pass and the output is in out-luma.json.

Setup: I used the fake luma device, but its canvas context's getCurrentFramebuffer runs luma's real WebGPUCanvasContext.prototype._createDepthStencilAttachment (node_modules/@luma.gl/webgpu/dist/adapter/webgpu-canvas-context.js:173-190). That method keeps one depth slot and destroys the stored texture whenever the format differs. It is driven through the real LumaRhiDevice. In one runFrame I ran pass A on swapchainWithDepth('depth24plus'), then pass B on swapchainWithDepth('depth24plus-stencil8'), then pass A2 on the first target again.

Recorded native pass.begin depth views:
- A = depthTex#0(depth24plus)
- B = depthTex#1(depth24plus-stencil8)
- A2 = depthTex#0(depth24plus)

B's acquisition destroyed depthTex#0. The frame was still submitted (runFrame returned true, no diagnostics), so passes A and A2 go to queue.submit with a destroyed texture. On a real GPU that is a validation error and the command buffer is dropped. A2 reuses the dead view because LumaSwapchainTarget.passViews (LumaRhiDevice.ts:496-505) caches it for the frame. Without that cache, A2 would re-acquire and destroy B's texture instead, so the conflict is still there.

NullRhiDevice (NullRhiDevice.ts:709-724) runs the same sequence with no error: it makes an independent NullTexture per format, which is what the RhiFrame.swapchainWithDepth contract implies (RhiDevice.ts:164-167). The Null/luma parity gap is real.

Game impact: none today. The only caller is WebGPURenderer.ts:343 (`frame.swapchainWithDepth(STENCIL_DEPTH_FORMAT)`), and STENCIL_DEPTH_FORMAT is the single constant 'depth24plus-stencil8' (Pipelines.ts:24). The MSAA path (WebGPURenderer.ts:342, swapchainMultisampled) uses RHI-owned depth textures, not the canvas slot. The other getCurrentFramebuffer call (LumaRhiDevice.ts:607) passes depthStencilFormat:false, which leaves the slot alone. luma also recreates the slot in preferredDepthFormat on configure/resize (webgpu-canvas-context.js:97), but that happens outside frame recording. The first in-frame acquisition just rebuilds it in stencil8 once, so nothing destroyed is referenced by a submitted pass.

Severity: low. This is an API/contract hazard and a Null/luma parity gap, and no game path reaches it. It is not a divergence from master for the game.
primary.fix_suggestion:
Smallest fix that keeps both backends in step: in both LumaRhiDevice.runFrame's and NullRhiDevice.runFrame's swapchainWithDepth closures, record the first depth format requested in the current frame. If a later call in the same frame asks for a different format, throw RhiError('unsupported', 'one canvas depth format per frame') (a check against a per-frame lastFormat is enough). The Null backend then rejects exactly what the luma backend cannot do.

Fuller alternative: make LumaSwapchainTarget own its depth texture per format, the way LumaMsaaSwapchainTarget does with depthTex. It would get the color view from getCurrentFramebuffer({depthStencilFormat:false}) and use its own device-created depth texture, resized from getDrawingBufferSize, which honours the RhiDevice.ts:164 contract.

Neither option changes game output, since the game only uses 'depth24plus-stencil8'.

confirmed.title: pushDebugGroup/popDebugGroup do not check for an open pass; on WebGPU this invalidates the whole command buffer
confirmed.description: `LumaCommandList.pushDebugGroup` and `popDebugGroup` forward straight to the lazily wrapped luma encoder, which forwards to the native GPUCommandEncoder. They skip `assertNoOpenPass`, which copyBufferToBuffer and copyTextureToTexture both call (lines 922, 942). Under the WebGPU spec, calling an encoder method while a render or compute pass is open (encoder state 'locked') invalidates the encoder. finish() then returns an invalid command buffer and the submit fails. NullRhiDevice (lines 417-423) does not check this either, so node tests cannot catch it.
confirmed.reference: WebGPU spec, 'validate the encoder state' (locked → invalidate encoder); LumaRhiDevice.ts:922/942 (copies call assertNoOpenPass); node_modules/@luma.gl/webgpu/dist/adapter/resources/webgpu-command-encoder.js pushDebugGroup → this.handle.pushDebugGroup
confirmed.failure_scenario: commands.beginRenderPass(...) followed by commands.pushDebugGroup('x') before pass.end(). The Null device logs it fine. On a real device the frame's command buffer becomes invalid, runFrame still returns true, and the canvas shows nothing for that frame.
confirmed.game_impact: None. The only caller is RenderGraph.execute (RenderGraph.ts:344-346), which calls these between passes, and RenderGraph is not used by the game or engine2d (no importer under src/ outside rhi). Low.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Call `this.assertNoOpenPass('pushDebugGroup')` and `this.assertNoOpenPass('popDebugGroup')` in both LumaCommandList and NullCommandList.

primary.reasoning:
I confirmed the missing guard with a repro. The WebGPU consequence itself needs a real GPU, so I could only check it against the spec.

What the repro shows: I ran runFrame with a render pass open on both LumaRhiDevice (backed by the fakeLumaDevice) and NullRhiDevice. On both, pushDebugGroup('x') and popDebugGroup() are accepted, but copyBufferToBuffer throws the assertNoOpenPass error.

The code matches the report:
- LumaRhiDevice.ts:960-966 forwards straight to this.encoder, the lazily created luma CommandEncoder, with no assertNoOpenPass.
- copyBufferToBuffer (line 922), copyTextureToTexture (line 942) and _submit all call assertNoOpenPass.
- luma's webgpu-command-encoder.js:152-156 passes pushDebugGroup/popDebugGroup through to the native GPUCommandEncoder (this.handle.pushDebugGroup).
- NullRhiDevice.ts:417-423 only logs the call.

Under the WebGPU spec, calling an encoder method while a pass is open (encoder state 'locked') invalidates the encoder. finish() then returns an invalid command buffer, and the submit produces a validation error. Node tests cannot show this part.

Game impact: none. The only callers are in RenderGraph.execute (src/rendering/rhi/graph/RenderGraph.ts:344-346). It calls them between passes (runPass opens and ends its own pass), so even that caller is correct. Nothing under src/ outside src/rendering/rhi imports RenderGraph; my grep found no importers. engine2d and the game never call pushDebugGroup or popDebugGroup. Pixi 8.17 and master have no equivalent API, so there is no parity divergence. This is a missing defensive check on an unused API, so severity is low.
primary.fix_suggestion:
Add the same guard the copies use:
- In LumaCommandList (src/rendering/rhi/backends/luma/LumaRhiDevice.ts:960-966), call `this.assertNoOpenPass('pushDebugGroup')` as the first line of pushDebugGroup, and `this.assertNoOpenPass('popDebugGroup')` in popDebugGroup.
- Put the same two calls in NullCommandList.pushDebugGroup and popDebugGroup (src/rendering/rhi/backends/null/NullRhiDevice.ts:417-423), so node tests catch the misuse.
- Optionally, add a unit test: calling pushDebugGroup inside an open render pass should throw RhiError 'invalid-usage' on both backends.

confirmed.title: Container.removeChildren(begin, end) with begin > 0 does not reproduce Pixi 8.17's removeItems behaviour (the game never calls it with arguments)
confirmed.description: engine2d removes exactly `end - begin` children with `this.children.splice(beginIndex, range)`. Pixi 8.17 calls `removeItems(this.children, beginIndex, end)`. The third parameter of removeItems is a remove COUNT, so Pixi takes `end` items out of the array (clamped to the array length) starting at `begin`. It still returns and detaches only `end - begin` of them. The extra children leave `children` but keep `parent === this`, and they get no 'removed' or 'childRemoved' event. engine2d behaves the way the API is documented, which is not what Pixi actually does.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A container has 10 children and calls removeChildren(2, 5). Pixi: returns 3 children, 5 remain in `children`, and 2 orphans still have parent === container. engine2d: returns 3 and 7 remain. Repro: tmp/review/r4-scene-text-events/misc.test.ts (pixi left 5, engine2d left 7).
confirmed.game_impact: None today. Every game call site is the argument-free `removeChildren()` (grep `removeChildren([^)]` over src/ outside engine2d finds nothing). That path is identical in both. The difference only shows if future code passes a non-zero begin index.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Choose one of two options: (1) keep the correct semantics and state the difference in the file header, or (2) copy Pixi's removeItems call if bit-for-bit Pixi parity is required. Option 1 is recommended because nothing in the game depends on the Pixi bug.

primary.reasoning:
The finding holds. At src/engine2d/scene/Container.ts:482, engine2d calls `this.children.splice(beginIndex, end - beginIndex)`. Pixi 8.17 calls `removeItems(this.children, beginIndex, end)` at node_modules/pixi.js/lib/scene/container/container-mixins/childrenHelperMixin.mjs:17. The third argument of removeItems is a remove count (node_modules/pixi.js/lib/utils/data/removeItems.mjs:2-13), and it is clamped to length - startIdx. So Pixi drops `end` items from `children` but only detaches and returns `end - begin` of them.

I ran a side-by-side vitest repro against the real 'pixi.js' package: 10 children, then removeChildren(2, 5).
- Pixi returned 3 children. `children` kept the children originally at indices [0,1,7,8,9]. The children at indices 5 and 6 are orphans: they are gone from `children` but still have parent === container, and they got no 'removed' event.
- engine2d returned 3 children and kept [0,1,5,6,7,8,9]. It has no orphans. The 'removed' events [4,3,2] match Pixi.

The divergence only appears when begin > 0 and there are enough items after the removed range. With begin = 0, count = end is the same as range = end, so both behave identically.

Game impact:
- All 26 removeChildren call sites under src/ outside src/engine2d take no arguments, which is the same as (0, length) and behaves identically.
- The only call inside engine2d that passes arguments, src/engine2d/scene/Container.ts:1494 `removeChildren(0, this.children.length)`, also uses begin = 0, so it is identical too.
- The game never reaches the diverging path. engine2d's behaviour is the documented API contract, and Pixi's is an upstream bug that corrupts the tree. Severity: low.
primary.fix_suggestion: Do not copy Pixi's bug, because it leaves orphans with a stale parent. Keep the `splice(beginIndex, range)` call at Container.ts:482 and add a comment there, or in the file header, saying the branch deliberately differs from Pixi 8.17's `removeItems(children, begin, end)`. That Pixi call over-removes `end` items when begin > 0. The difference is unobservable for begin === 0, which covers every game call site. If strict bit-parity is required instead, replace the splice with `this.children.splice(beginIndex, Math.min(end, this.children.length - beginIndex))`. That reproduces the removeItems count clamp, but it creates orphaned children, so it is not recommended.

confirmed.title: shaderTwins guard ignores integer constants, top-level declarations, signs and constant order, so one-sided twin edits pass
confirmed.description: The round-3 GLSL/WGSL twin guard compares a sorted multiset of decimal-point literals for each function. `nums()` matches only literals with a '.' or an exponent, and drops 0 and 1. As a result: (a) integer literals are never compared, including loop bounds (`i <= 128` in lightingCore, `i < 12` in breathingShade) and integer light-kind codes; (b) declarations before the first function are dropped by fnsGlsl/fnsWgsl, including LC_PI, LC_LUMA, LC_POINT..LC_LINE and BURN_NEVER; (c) minus signs are not captured; (d) because the list is sorted, swapping two constants between expressions is invisible. Separately, if a marker is renamed, `sl()` (line 28) silently slices from index -1 instead of failing.
confirmed.reference: src/rendering/shaderTwins.test.ts:28 (sl), :46-47 (nums), fnsGlsl/fnsWgsl only index from the first `fn`/typed function; twins: src/rendering/lighting/lightingCore.glsl:31-40 vs lightingCore.wgsl:40-49, breathingShade.glsl:52,57 vs .wgsl:58,63
confirmed.failure_scenario: Repro tmp/review/r4-test-guards/twinsBlind.test.ts, run with the guard's own helpers on the real sources. The guard still reports 'equal' after each of these WGSL-only edits: breathing displacement iterations 12→4; LC_LUMA changed to (0.299,0.587,0.114); LC_PI=3.0; LC_SPOT and LC_AREA codes swapped; march bound 128→64; `(0.5 / LC_PI)`→`(-0.5 / LC_PI)`. All 4 repro tests pass, which means all of these blind spots exist.
confirmed.game_impact: The game runs only the WGSL side. The GLSL twins feed the burn, breathing, beam and bolt workbenches (their WebGL pages). Any drift would make workbench previews differ from the game, with no runtime effect on the game. The guard is weaker than its header claims.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Also compare integer literals, with sign, per function in source order. Include the top-level const/#define block as a pseudo-function. Make `sl()` throw when a marker is missing.

primary.reasoning:
I wrote my own repro that copies the guard's helpers (sl/strip/fnsGlsl/fnsWgsl/nums from src/rendering/shaderTwins.test.ts:28-47) word for word. It applies them to the real twins: the LIGHTING_CORE slice of lightingCore.glsl vs LC_WGSL, and breathingShade.glsl vs breathingShade.wgsl. All 8 tests pass.

1. **Baseline:** the unmodified twins pass the guard.
2. **Sanity check:** changing a float inside a function, `(0.5 / LC_PI)` to `(0.25 / LC_PI)`, IS caught. So the repro reproduces the guard's real behaviour.
3. **Missed changes:** the guard still reports equal after each of these WGSL-only edits:
   - march bound `i <= 128` → `i <= 64` (lightingCore.wgsl:172)
   - breathing iterations `i < 12` → `i < 4` (breathingShade.wgsl:58)
   - `LC_PI` set to 3.0
   - `LC_LUMA` changed to (0.299, 0.587, 0.114) (lightingCore.wgsl:40-41 sit before the first `fn`, so fnsWgsl never sees them)
   - `LC_SPOT`/`LC_AREA` codes swapped 1↔2 (integer top-level consts)
   - sign flip `(0.5/LC_PI)` → `(-0.5/LC_PI)`
4. **sl():** when a marker is missing it slices from indexOf = -1 and returns a string instead of throwing.

Why it happens, from the code:
- The `nums` regex requires a '.' or an exponent, so integers are never compared.
- Minus signs are not captured.
- 0 and 1 are filtered out.
- The list is sorted, so the order of constants is lost.
- fnsGlsl/fnsWgsl only index from the first function header, so top-level declarations are dropped.

Game impact: none at runtime. This is a test-only guard. The game compiles only the WGSL side through the engine2d/RHI path. The GLSL twins (burnShade.glsl, breathingShade.glsl, vfxBeamGlsl/vfxBoltGlsl cores) only feed the workbench WebGL pages, and this change does not alter rendering output. The only risk is that a future one-sided edit goes undetected, which would make workbench previews differ from the game. Nothing diverges from master today (the baseline passes), so severity is low.
primary.fix_suggestion:
In src/rendering/shaderTwins.test.ts:
(1) sl(): throw when indexOf(begin) or indexOf(end) is -1, or when end < begin. Or reuse sliceWgsl from wgslChunks.ts, if it already validates.
(2) nums(): match every numeric literal, integers included, with an optional leading unary minus. For example `/(?<![\w.])(-?\s*(?:\d*\.\d+(?:[eE][-+]?\d+)?|\d+\.?(?:[eE][-+]?\d+)?))/g`, after stripping type generics and f/u/i suffixes. Keep source order (drop the .sort()) and stop filtering out 0 and 1. Or, if 0.0/1.0 spelling differences between the twins are too noisy, normalise them instead of dropping them.
(3) In fnsGlsl/fnsWgsl, add the text before the first function as a pseudo-entry, e.g. '<prelude>'. Compare its literals too, after mapping `#define NAME v` and `const NAME: T = v;` to a name→value table, so LC_PI, LC_LUMA, the LC_POINT..LC_LINE codes and BURN_NEVER are checked by name.
Keep the KNOWN_EQUIVALENT exemption for lcSpotLight. Re-run and add further exemptions only for verified-equivalent spelling differences, e.g. literal folding written with f suffixes.

confirmed.title: noPixiInRuntime guard skips tools/parallax_editor (already migrated to engine2d) and misses some import forms
confirmed.description: The guard scans only `src` and `tools/anim_preview`. tools/parallax_editor was also moved off Pixi on this branch: master tools/parallax_editor/main.ts:1 `from 'pixi.js'`, now `from '@src/engine2d'`. Because pixi.js is still a devDependency (package.json:58), a regression back to Pixi there would build and run with nothing flagging it. The check is also line-based (line 28), which leaves three blind spots: `} from` with the module name on the next line; a template-literal dynamic import (import(`pixi.js`)), since the regex requires ' or "; and any line that starts with a block comment such as `/* keep */ import ... from 'pixi.js'`, which is skipped as a comment.
confirmed.reference: src/engine2d/noPixiInRuntime.test.ts:22 (PIXI_IMPORT), :28 (comment-line skip), :36/:41 (only src and tools/anim_preview scanned); git show 5f5a639:tools/parallax_editor/main.ts line 1

confirmed.suggested_fix: Add 'tools/parallax_editor' (and any other tool that aliases @src) to the scanned roots. Match on the whole file with a multiline regex that also accepts backticks, and strip only real comments rather than whole lines starting with /*.

Then change pixiImports so it matches against the whole file instead of each line. First strip real comments with `text.replace(/\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//g, '').replace(/(^|[^:'"`])\/\/.*$/gm, '$1')`. Then use a global regex that allows whitespace and newlines and accepts all three quote styles: `/(?:from|import|require)\s*\(?\s*['"`]pixi\.js(?:\/[^'"`]*)?['"`]/g`. Map each match's offset back to a line number for the error message. Also consider matching `@pixi/` package names.

confirmed.title: TextureStyle regression test asserts behaviour that differs from master's WebGL path after renderer re-creation or device restore
confirmed.description: The third test says the sampler is built from the parameters in effect when the key was first computed. It changes scaleMode/addressMode without update(), builds a new renderer (standing in for device-loss recovery), and expects the stale linear/clamp sampler (lines 84-91). Master runs Pixi WebGL with `_useSeparateSamplers = false`. There, sampler state is written to each GL texture from the current `source.style` fields whenever the GL texture is created (initSource → updateStyle → applyStyleParams). After a context restore (contextChange) or a GC unload and re-upload, the GL texture is re-created and the current fields apply. So on master the new renderer or restored context would sample nearest/repeat. The test documents the branch's key-cached model as if it were master behaviour.
confirmed.reference: node_modules/pixi.js/lib/rendering/renderers/gl/texture/GlTextureSystem.mjs:28 (_useSeparateSamplers = false), :53 (contextChange resets GL state), :160/:164-171 (initSource/onStyleChange → updateStyle → applyStyleParams(source.style …))
confirmed.failure_scenario: A source is drawn once (linear). Then `source.scaleMode = 'nearest'` is set without style.update(). Then the device is lost and restored, or the source is GC-unloaded and re-uploaded. Master (WebGL) samples nearest from then on. The branch keeps the cached key and linear sampler, and the test enforces that.
confirmed.game_impact: I found none. The game's style writes without update() happen before the texture is first drawn: UITextures.ts:41 (paper addressMode after Assets.load), backgroundSway.ts:368 (ids scaleMode), HUD.ts:1162 (followed by source.update()). Both models give the same result for these. The test only matters if future code changes style after first use.

primary.reasoning:
The divergence is real. I reproduced it in node by running the two sides next to each other.

Master side: I built the real Pixi 8.17 GlTextureSystem (exported from 'pixi.js') over a fake WebGL2 context that records every call.
- A BufferImageSource is bound once. It gets TEXTURE_MAG_FILTER LINEAR and TEXTURE_WRAP_S CLAMP_TO_EDGE.
- I then set source.scaleMode='nearest' and addressMode='repeat' without update().
- I simulated webglcontextrestored by calling sys.contextChange(gl) and then re-bound the source. The re-created GL texture gets TEXTURE_MAG_FILTER NEAREST and TEXTURE_WRAP_S REPEAT. The log shows mag=['LINEAR'(EMPTY),'NEAREST'] and wrapS=[...,'REPEAT'].
- The same thing happens after a GC unload (src.unload()) and re-bind: NEAREST.
- Why: GlTextureSystem._initSource calls updateStyle, which calls applyStyleParams(source.style…) and reads the current fields (GlTextureSystem.mjs:160 and :164-171; applyStyleParams.mjs:4-30). _useSeparateSamplers is false (:28), and contextChange drops all GL textures (:53-60).

Branch side: I used engine2d WebGPURenderer on a NullRhiDevice with the same steps and then `await rhi.loseDevice()`.
- After the restore, the sampler is recreated with magFilter 'linear' and addressModeU 'clamp-to-edge'.
- Why: GpuTextures.sampler() (src/engine2d/gpu/GpuTextures.ts:133-152) builds the sampler from style._keyFields. TextureStyle.ts:114-143 caches those fields until update(). GpuTextures.reset() (:180-188) clears the sampler map but not the style's cached fields.

So after a device restore or a GC re-upload, master samples with the current fields and the branch keeps the stale ones. src/engine2d/textures/TextureStyle.test.ts:67-91 enforces the branch model. The file header (lines 2-3, "master 的 WebGL 同理") reads as if the whole file matches master, so the test does document this divergence as though it were parity. The source comment at TextureStyle.ts:111-112 does admit that only changes made before first use match master.

Game impact: none. The only style writes in the game are:
- src/ui/UITextures.ts:41 (paper addressMode, set right after Assets.load and before any draw)
- src/rendering/backgroundSway.ts:368 (ids scaleMode='nearest', set right after load and before the texture is used by the sway pass)
- src/ui/HUD.ts:1162 (followed by source.update() at :1163)
All three happen before the key is first computed, or are followed by update(). Neither model differs for them. This only matters if future code changes a style after first use, without update(), and a device loss or texture GC then happens. Severity: low.
primary.fix_suggestion:
Cheapest fix (enough, since the game never hits this): reword the header of TextureStyle.test.ts and the title and comment of the third test. They should say this is a deliberate divergence from master's WebGL. On master, a re-created GL texture (after context restore or GC re-upload) gets the current style fields. The branch keeps the parameters that were in effect when the key was computed until update() is called. They should also say game code must call update() after changing a style that has already been drawn.

If exact master behaviour is wanted: add a non-emitting `TextureStyle._invalidateKey()` that sets _cachedKey and _cachedFields to null. Call it for source.style in GpuTextures.get() at the point where a new GPU texture entry is created (first use, re-creation after unload/GC, and after reset() on device restore). This mirrors master's initSource→updateStyle, which re-reads the current fields each time the texture is re-created. Then flip the expectations at TextureStyle.test.ts:89-90 to nearest/repeat. One caveat: WebGL applies the params per texture, but a style can be shared by several sources, so this re-keys every source that shares it. That matches master once all of them have been re-created after a restore.

primary.reasoning:
The coverage gap is real. No test under src or tools calls pipelinesReady or whenAllReady with anything other than an already-ready set: the only callers are src/engine2d/gpu/prewarmPipelines.test.ts lines 54, 75 and 108, which all do `pipelinesReady(1000) === true`. NullRhiDevice can only model a pipeline that is ready at once or one that rejects (failPipeline, NullRhiDevice.ts:59-60 and 119-126). It has no way to model a `ready` that never settles.

Master's deleted src/rendering/glProgramWarmup.test.ts did guard both cases: `whenReady(30)` is false while compiles are pending, and in '等待中销毁：立刻放行' destroy() during the wait makes `whenReady(60_000)` resolve false at once.

Repro, run with vitest in node on NullRhiDevice, wrapping rhi.createRenderPipeline so `ready` never settles:
(1) pipelinesReady(30) resolves false after about 31 ms. The current timeout race in Pipelines.ts:170-181 is correct, as the finding says.
(2) Calling pipelinesReady(500), then renderer.destroy() on the next microtask, resolves false only after about 501 ms. The wait runs to the full timeout; destroy does not release it.

So the branch not only lacks master's teardown guard, it also behaves differently on that path. Master's GlProgramWarmup.destroy() (master Game.ts:10335, reached from teardown) let the reveal gate go at once. On the branch, Pipelines.destroy() only calls reset(), which clears the map. The already-built Promise.allSettled keeps waiting until REVEAL_GATE_SHADER_TIMEOUT_MS, which is 15000 ms (Game.ts:287).

Game impact: the reveal gate runs on every scene load (Game.ts:2215-2226 calls renderer.app.renderer.pipelinesReady(15000)). If the game is torn down during a scene transition (Game.ts:10093 sets tearDownComplete, then renderer.destroy at 10269), the gate promise and its closures stay alive for up to 15 s before the tearDownComplete-guarded body runs. This is harmless apart from a transient retained closure and timer. In normal play the timeout path only matters if a pipeline stalls. The code is correct today and the gap is regression protection, so the severity is low.
primary.fix_suggestion:
1. Add an option to NullRhiDevice, for example `pendingPipeline?: (label: string) => boolean`, whose matching pipelines get a `ready` that never settles, so tests can model a pipeline that never finishes compiling.
2. In prewarmPipelines.test.ts, bring back master's two guards:
   (a) with a pending pipeline, `await renderer.pipelinesReady(20)` is false;
   (b) `const w = renderer.pipelinesReady(60_000); renderer.destroy(); expect(await w).toBe(false)`, finishing well under the timeout.
3. To match master's '等待中销毁：立刻放行', have Pipelines keep a set of active wait-resolvers (or an AbortController). Pipelines.destroy() should resolve them with false and clear their timers, so teardown does not leave the reveal-gate promise pending for REVEAL_GATE_SHADER_TIMEOUT_MS. reset() on device restore should keep its current behaviour: the rebuilt prewarm pipelines are awaited by the next gate.

coverage.coverage:
STATIC review of the post-fix GPU core (4dd11ca..HEAD, including perf commits 205a2e3/4076e7d and the R3 fix 37647fb), read file by file against Pixi 8.17 lib/*.mjs and master. All nine areas below matched Pixi. The only real mismatch is one low-severity API-edge divergence that the game never hits.

CHECKED AND EQUIVALENT:

1. Scratch reuse after the perf rewrite (FrameBuilder.ts)
- colorScratch, localScratch, filterScratch, batchTextureScratch and batchSamplerScratch are all copied into the Arena (writeUbo → packUbo) or into a fresh object-literal binding table before the next use. No DrawCmd keeps a reference to a scratch object.
- globalPush clones the projection and world matrices.
- BatchRecord objects replayed by the stencil pop re-read immutable data only.

2. ArenaRef fill-in timing
- Every ArenaRef goes through arenaRef(), from these callers: globalPush, drawUnbatched, drawCustom local/textureUniforms, snapshotGroup, updateFilterUniforms.
- bindUniformBuffer runs in upload() before record(). The buffer is always non-null when any draw exists; the NullRhi probe tmp/review/r4-gpu-core/probe.test.ts asserts this over 3 frames.
- snapshotGroup dedupe reclaims arena space correctly, and groupSlices is per builder and per render.
- runFrame and submit are synchronous (LumaRhiDevice.ts:1661/1718), so builder.commands and the state buffers cannot be overwritten before recording.
- Nested renders from onRender run before the outer state is used; nested renders during planning use states[depth].
- Multiple render() calls per frame (lighting, contactAo, shadowPrefix ping-pong) rewrite the uniform buffer with queue-ordered writeBuffer, so each submit sees its own data.

3. Pipeline fast path (Pipelines.ts)
- The state integer encodes every createRenderPipeline input: topology, blend, colour format, depth format, stencil (only when depth is set), colour mask and sample count, in 52 bits with no overlap. The program object and layout object are the outer keys.
- The slow key matches field for field. NON_BLENDABLE depends only on colour format, which is in the key.
- The layout cache is version-gated on addAttribute. The game adds attributes only before the first draw (CharacterLitSprite.ts:1211 in the constructor).
- Offset defaulting to 0 matches Pixi (Pixi uses attribute.offset; `start` is unused).

4. TextureStyle._key caching
- Matches Pixi `_resourceId`, and samplers are built from _keyFields.
- The game changes style fields only before first use or followed by update(): UITextures.ts:41, HUD.ts:1162-1164, backgroundSway.ts:368.

5. Pool borrowing and abort()
- Every take is paired with a return: filterPush/filterPop, the applyFiltersToTexture temp, and the alpha-mask texture, including the skip paths.
- abort returns only outstanding textures, with no double return.
- NullRhi probe: a filter that throws on 3 consecutive frames leaves the TexturePool count unchanged, and the next frame and an RT render still work.

6. GC vs live references
- Collection runs only at the outermost postrender, after submit. lastUsed is updated on every get(), including render-target binds.
- Pool, RenderTexture, Video and BufferImage sources have autoGarbageCollect false. Buffers are rebuilt from the full CPU data.
- releaseTargets is chained through onRelease.

7. contextChange completeness
- It clears targets, pipelines and shaders (including prewarm, then rebuilds prewarm), buffers, textures and samplers, and the per-state vertex, index and uniform buffers.
- Only CPU state is kept (layouts, stencilTargets, pool). No game code outside engine2d holds RHI objects; only debug/gpuPanelDiagnostics uses gpuTextureOf.

8. Masks
- The stencil push/pop sequence and replay match StencilMaskPipe and GlStencilSystem, including the per-target mask stack and MASK_ACTIVE after pop.
- The alpha-mask sequence (break, pushMaskBegin, collect, break, pushMaskEnd; renderMask push/pop target plus globalUniforms offset/worldColor; the internal sprite's worldTransform tx/ty) matches AlphaMaskPipe.
- The colour-mask stack matches ColorMaskPipe. The GL (8=R) to WebGPU (1=R) bit reversal is correct. MaskFilter and mask.wgsl match Pixi apart from the documented extra uMaskSampler.
- All game masks are Graphics, so only the stencil path is used (UIScrollView, InventoryUI:465, DevModeUI, DialogueUI:811, ObjectExamineScene:401).
- Probe: a blur+alpha filter inside a stencil-masked container on the canvas gives the expected passes, stencil loads and refs (filter output drawn 'active' ref 1, mask removal 'remove' ref 1, after-pop draws 'active' ref 0).

9. Filters, roundPixels and prewarm
- FilterSystem push/pop/applyFilter/_updateFilterUniforms were checked line by line (globalFrame, the outputTexture.z = -1 WebGPU equivalent, resolution/antialias inheritance, previous-filter offsets).
- uRoundFlipY is 0 only for the canvas and 1 for RenderTexture, filter input, alpha-mask and flop targets. The global uniform is always pushed right after binding its target. No game or engine2d WGSL outside batchShader uses roundPixels.
- The GLOBAL_LAYOUT tail field keeps the 128-byte struct size for game shaders that declare only the first four fields.
- Batcher packing and breaks match Pixi. Unbatched graphics use groupBlendMode, as in GraphicsPipe.
- Prewarm keys equal draw keys (depth null and depth+'disabled', colorMask 15, swapchain plus bgra8unorm).

NOT CHECKED OR OUT OF SCOPE:
- RHI internals: bind-group cache, MSAA swapchain.
- The Text/HTMLText texture lifecycle under GC.
- Whether prewarm hits for draws after a mask pops in the same frame (performance only, documented design).
- Browser or GPU execution (static round).

Also seen but not reported (the game never hits them): globalPush uses `??` where Pixi uses `||` for worldColor (differs only for a root with tint 0x000000 and alpha < 1/255), and resolveTarget treats any HTMLCanvasElement as the renderer's own canvas.

Checked at HEAD, static only, against luma.gl 9.4.2 source and the WebGPU spec. The only node run was `npx vitest run src/rendering/rhi` (8 files, 99 tests, all pass). I found no game-path divergence or regression in this slice. Found equivalent / correct:

(1) Native encoder plus lazy luma wrapper (commit 2855653). The luma WebGPUCommandEncoder is built with `handle: native`, so copyBufferToBuffer, copyTextureToTexture, beginComputePass (WebGPUComputePass is passed this.handle) and the debug groups all record on the same GPUCommandEncoder, in call order. No luma path uses device.commandEncoder or writeBufferViaCommandEncoder, so no transient upload buffers are destroyed before submit. `_submit` does finish → destroy the wrapper → queue.submit. `_abandon` ends the open native pass and drops the encoder. The old luma WebGPURenderPass wrapper added no behaviour beyond labels, logs and stats, so bypassing it loses nothing. The game only uses render passes, queue writes, mipgen and readTexture; copies, compute and debug groups are unused.

(2) Error scopes. luma push/popErrorScope are no-ops when debug is off. captureErrors pushes internal and validation scopes on the native GPUDevice and pops them in LIFO order, including when creation throws. A pop that fails on a lost device resolves to null. Everything else goes through uncapturederror → onError → report.

(3) Bind-group cache (LumaBindingPlan). The key is the RHI object identity per declared binding, plus offset/size for buffer ranges, plus the texture's current luma sampler when `<tex>Sampler` is declared. This matches what luma's getBindGroupEntries actually binds (texture.view.handle plus texture.sampler.handle, same group). Destroyed resources fail assertAlive before the cache lookup. New or recreated resources are new WeakMap keys. Pipelines are recreated after restore, so plans are too, and the bind-group factory is per luma device. The 1024-entry reset is harmless. The per-pass boundGroups / boundPipeline / vertex / index dedupe is correct under WebGPU persistence rules, including skipped (failed) pipelines. Two scripted scans of game WGSL: no paired sampler sits in a different group from its texture, and every paired `uXSampler` name has a TS provider. `uTexSampler` is the one name with zero TS references; I did not locate its declaring shader, so that call path is unconfirmed.

(4) Adapter wrapper. It only adds requiredLimits.maxTextureDimension2D equal to the adapter's value. The selectAdapter map takes props.adapters over preregistered ones, and each createDevice or restore requests a fresh adapter.

(5) Device loss and restore. Stale lost signals from replaced or destroyed devices are ignored. releaseCanvas runs before the new configure. _invalidateResources skips the untracked canvas targets. MSAA and depth canvas targets and the mip generator are rebuilt for the new device. Caps and info are refreshed in place, the stored swapchain size is re-applied (luma's initial drawing buffer size is canvas.width), and destroy during a retry is handled. untilLost removes itself on settle and rejects on loss.

(6) Canvas views. Views are cached per frame and reset in _beginFrame/_endFrame, including for depth targets created lazily mid-frame. Resize goes through setDrawingBufferSize → _configureDevice at the first acquire of the next frame, with autoResize off. MSAA color is shared per sample count and rebuilt by generation. Level-0 views are used for multi-mip attachments and resolve targets and are destroyed with the target. luma Framebuffer.destroy does not destroy caller-supplied attachments.

(7) Mip generator. Matches Pixi GpuMipmapGenerator (flipped UV, linear min, one encoder, one submit) and is reset on restore. The HUD atlas is the game's only autoGenerateMipmaps user.

(8) readTexture. Row padding is stripped, staging is destroyed in finally, and COPY_SRC is required.

(9) Null vs luma validation. Usage bits, destroyed checks, format and sample-count match, bindings and paired samplers, vertex streams and index buffer, the canvas armed check, and the in-flight write check are all equivalent. Neither backend checks 4-byte writeBuffer alignment, but engine2d pads (GpuBuffers.writeTail).

Not verified: real-GPU behaviour of mapAsync / onSubmittedWorkDone on a lost device when readTexture is called during the lost window (it relies on the browser rejecting); RenderGraph / RgTransientPool internals beyond a skim (not used by the game); luma's WGSL scanner on every game shader (covered by the existing render_parity cases).

     All pass. The only difference is the trailing `_pad0`/`_pad1` in the contact-AO struct, which is harmless.
   - The existing repo guards all pass at HEAD: vfxWgsl, charLightingWgsl, entityShadingWgsl, burnWgsl, sceneLightingWgsl, shaderTwins, vfxPipelineSpecs and entityHierarchy.
   - Every runtime texture swap also swaps its sampler: setLitShaderTexture, parkLitShaders/rebind, CharacterShadingFilter.setNormalTexture, the EntityShadow cast `uTexture`, BackgroundDebugFilter set/unbind, water set*Texture, LitBackground.setSway, SceneLightingPass `uSurfMask`, shadowPrefix `uPrev` and the contactAo composite. SceneLightingPass `uPL*`/`uSkyao` are textureLoad-only.
   - The only texture style change in the game that could affect a shader (`idsTex` set to nearest in backgroundSway) happens before its sampler is captured.
   - No UniformGroup uses `isStatic`, and no boolean values are written into uniforms.
   - Every GL shader or filter has a GPU twin except UnifiedCharacterShader, which is already known and disabled.
   - The `burnImg` → `burnUniforms` rename has no other readers. The `uBeamAlong` reorder only matters to WGSL.
   - All `BufferImageSource`s with an alpha channel are explicitly `no-premultiply-alpha`, so the raw upload in engine2d matches master's GL upload.

4. **contactAo clearMask.** A NullRhiDevice repro (tmp/review/r4-game-side/clear.test.ts) shows that an empty-container `render(clear: true)` opens a clearing pass on the RenderTexture, and the following caster render uses `load`. That is equivalent to master's `bind(rt, true)`.

5. **WebGL assumptions remaining in src.**
   - There are no `renderer.type`/`'webgl'` branches in logic; `DepthDebugVisualizer` only logs the type.
   - There are no GPU readbacks in the game. `uiShotHarness` is dev-only and awaits the async extract.
   - The only `gl_FragCoord` uses are GiBouncePass (unified path, disabled) and gatherRT, which is only reachable with uMode 0, and the game clamps mode to at least 1 (CharacterLightingSystem:579/1112).
   - There are no 32-bit float textures (which would need float32-filterable).
   - No Pixi-internal fields are accessed via casts.

6. **Tools.**
   - anim_preview and parallax_editor catch init errors, and parallax_editor/index.html provides `#canvas-host`.
   - scene_sweep reports `renderer.name`, which is `'webgpu'`.

**Intentional behaviour changes, not reported**
- BackgroundDebugFilter now declares `uGroundMin`, `uGroundMax` and `uHasGroundTex` up front. Master only assigned them after construction, so the F2 collision debug view with a ground field was broken or grey on master and now works. This is debug-only.
- The anim_preview GIF export now extracts the full screen frame instead of master's stage-bounds crop. This is tool-only.

**Not checked**
- WGSL numeric equivalence beyond the twin and layout guards (that is the render_parity and shader slices).
- engine2d internals such as filter `uOutputTexture` and upload semantics (other slices).
- Real-GPU pipeline timing of the reveal gate.

This was a static review: no browsers or A/B runs. Repros are under .claude/review-repros/engine2d-r4/r4-test-guards/: twinsBlind.test.ts, noPixiGuard.test.ts and fracRes.test.ts, all passing.

(1) Regression tests added in 4dd11ca..HEAD. I read these and judged each one to assert Pixi/master behaviour, to fail if its fix were reverted, and to be deterministic, apart from the TextureStyle case reported above:
- gpuGc.test.ts: compares GCSystem.defaultOptions with PIXI, checks FillGradient autoGarbageCollect against a PIXI FillGradient, checks Buffer and Geometry.destroy index buffers against PIXI. It uses a mocked performance.now, so it is deterministic.
- roundPixelsTarget.test.ts: builds the master row from PIXI calculateProjection(flipY=!isRoot) with f32 evaluation. Before the fix, flip=0 would give the wrong tie, so it fails on revert.
- prewarmPipelines.test.ts: the R2-2 stencil-variant case fails on revert because the depth-format pipeline is missing. The R3 restore case fails on revert because the rebuild count comparison (perPrewarm×2) breaks.
- textureLimit.test.ts / LumaRhiDevice.limits.test.ts: compare with PIXI TexturePool; check requiredLimits; check that the pool texture is returned.
- EventEmitter.test.ts: compares against eventemitter3 directly.
- cullInactive.test.ts: compares against PIXI.Culler with visible=false.
- masks.test.ts: compares against PIXI mask type choice, calculateSpriteMatrix/TextureMatrix and the mask.wgsl source.
- VideoSource.test.ts: runs the same story against PIXI.VideoSource and documents its one intentional difference.
- HTMLText.test.ts: the reference moved from WEBGPU to WEBGL, which is correct for master, and resolutions 1.25/2.5 were added.
- lumaMapping and BlurFilter changes: additive only.
- deviceLoss tests: rely on a bounded number of setTimeout(0) turns. I judged that deterministic given the single-timeout fake recreate.

I also spot-read the renderHotPath and renderSemantics structure. The pipeline fast key encodes all 9 PipelineKey fields in 52 bits, and reset() clears the fast map, which the test covers.

(2) Tests changed vs master (git diff 5f5a639 HEAD):
- 19 test files were modified. The only changes are pixi.js→engine2d imports, vi.mock paths re-pointed to '../engine2d' (I verified the mocked module is the same one backgroundSway.ts and LitBackground.ts import), the prepareTree replacement for updateRenderGroupTransforms, and the createLitShader signature.
- No removed expects apart from the two deleted files. No it.skip, .todo, .only, .fails or conditional early returns were added anywhere in src tests.
- The vitest config (vite.config.ts test block) is unchanged vs master.
- Two files were deleted. vfxGlPrograms.test.ts has an equivalent replacement: vfxPipelineSpecs.test.ts covers both GLSL and WGSL gatherRT, the getter coverage and the attribute check. glProgramWarmup.test.ts has only a partial replacement (reported above).

(3) Parity harnesses:
- engine2d_parity: 29 cases. Tolerance is 0–2/255, with the +1e-6 check. maxBadPixels defaults to 0. Errors on either side count as 'error', not 'pass'.
- None of those 29 cases cover: the canvas/root target (every case renders offscreen), MSAA, HTMLText, ImageSource/CanvasSource textures (canvasTexture is defined but unused), mipmaps, video, or fractional resolution.
- render_parity: resolution is fixed at 1. The refKnownError path marks a case 'pass' without comparing pixels whenever the reference side throws for any reason; it does not check that the message matches. This is used only by the F2 collision-view debug case (60_minigame_debug.ts:222), so the impact is low.
- The ref-side fallback plugin only fills in modules that are missing from the master tree. A branch-only named export requested from a master module fails loudly rather than vacuously.
- Neither parity tool is wired into npm scripts or the build gates; both are run by hand.

(4) noPixiInRuntime guard:
- src currently has no pixi, @pixi or node_modules/pixi imports; I checked all 779 .ts files.
- The guard handles static, export-from, `import(`, `require(` and subpath imports.
- It misses the cases reported above.
- tools/parallax_editor typechecks cleanly with its own tsconfig.

Side checks with no divergence found:
- Fractional-resolution sizing (RenderTexture.create/resize, TexturePool.getOptimalTexture) is equal to Pixi at 1.25, 1.5, 1.75 and 2.25.
- Filter-bounds rounding code in FrameBuilder.ts:1136-1137 is identical to Pixi FilterSystem.mjs:585-587.

Not checked: pixel-level render_parity case contents, i.e. whether any of the 176 cases draws an all-empty frame on both sides (this needs a browser run). Also not checked: the rhi_smoke real-device cases.

# Completeness critique of review round 4: gaps and next-round tasks

Round 4 left four areas nobody examined: the path from engine2d `Buffer` objects to GPU buffers used by the dynamic VFX meshes, how canvas text is drawn to pixels, how gradients and legacy blur look in the final image, and anything that only shows up at runtime. Every task below comes from a gap I confirmed by grepping. None of them is a finding yet.

## Gaps I checked and closed (do not re-assign)

- **Canvas alpha mode.** `src/engine2d/gpu/createRenderer.ts:20` sets `'opaque'` when the background alpha is 1. This matches Pixi `GlContextSystem.mjs:65`. The game uses an opaque `#1a1a2e` background.
- **r8unorm upload alignment.** WebGL defaults to 4-byte row alignment for uploads, and Pixi 8.17 never changes it for buffer uploads (`glUploadBufferImageResource.mjs`). engine2d writes rows tightly packed.
  - The probe `validTex` width is always a multiple of 4 (`CharacterLightingSystem.ts:612`).
  - `skyVisibilityTexture` is only read by the disabled unified path (`Game.ts:6595`).
  - `rgba16float` and `rgba8` rows are always aligned. No divergence.
- **Rendering a container directly.** `WebGPURenderer.ts:200-216` matches Pixi `AbstractRenderer.mjs:92-99` and `RenderGroupSystem.render`: the same visible gate, the same transform default, and colour taken from the container itself because its parent is detached. Pixi does not check the root's own display status either (`RenderGroupSystem.mjs:137`), so culled-root behaviour is the same.
- **`BlurFilter.apply` with zero strength.** The x/y branches are identical to `BlurFilter.mjs:41-58`.
- **`uTexSampler`** appears only in RHI tests and `tools/engine2d_parity/cases/20_mesh.ts`, never in game code.
- **PlayerLoop.** It is added to the ticker at NORMAL priority during init (`Application.ts:115`). No game component has hooks, so the order of game ticker callbacks is unchanged.

## Next-round tasks, in priority order

**P1. Dynamic `Buffer` → GPU upload path, used by every VFX mesh every frame.** No round-4 slice read `src/engine2d/gpu/GpuBuffers.ts` or `src/engine2d/shader/Buffer.ts` for upload behaviour; gpu-core only covered garbage collection and device restore.
- **Game users:**
  - `VfxBatchMesh.ts:130-134`, `VfxBoltBatchMesh.ts:105`, `VfxPlateBatchMesh.ts`.
  - `VfxBeamView.ts:121-135`: the index buffer is rewritten only when the hull point count changes, and it switches blend between add, screen and normal at :157.
  - `backgroundSway.ts:1039-1048,1393,1476`: `Uint32` index buffer.
  - `breathingOverlayMesh.ts`.
- **What to check against Pixi `GpuBufferSystem.mjs` and `GlBufferSystem.mjs`:**
  - Partial uploads with `update(sizeInBytes)` / `_uploadSize`.
  - `setDataWithSize` with a smaller array when `shrinkToFit` is false: the GPU buffer keeps its old size and the tail bytes are stale.
  - Swapping `data` for a new array of the same length.
  - Uploads where the byte length is not a multiple of 4 (`writeTail`).
  - Choosing `indexFormat` for `Uint16` vs `Uint32`.
  - Draw count when the index buffer is larger than the live data (the beam draws a zero-filled tail).
- **How to test:** a NullRhi repro that records `writeBuffer` offsets and lengths over a grow → shrink → partial-update sequence.

**P2. Canvas text drawn to pixels.** Round-4 scene-text-events covered only the texture lifecycle. `tools/engine2d_parity` has one text case (`60_graphics_text.ts`), and it has no `trim`, `letterSpacing`, `padding`, `whiteSpace`, `fontVariant` or `textBaseline`, and no fractional resolution.
- **Game usage counts:**

  | Style option | Uses |
  |---|---|
  | `wordWrapWidth` | 105 |
  | `breakWords` | 82 |
  | `letterSpacing` | 72 |
  | `padding` | 44 |
  | `dropShadow` | 35 |
  | `stroke` | 23 |
  | `trim` | 16 |
  | `whiteSpace` | 15 |

- **Focus files:** `src/engine2d/text/canvas/*`, `text/utils/getTextureFromCanvas.ts`, `CanvasTextSystem.ts:57-125`.
- **What to check:**
  - Does `CanvasTextGenerator.test.ts` (3 test blocks) cover the game's actual style combinations (drop shadow + stroke + padding + trim) at resolutions 1.25, 1.5 and 2?
  - Is the text canvas upload premultiplied the same way Pixi's canvas upload is?
  - Text used directly for layout: `CanvasTextMetrics.measureText` in `clueSpans.ts:89-93`, `RichContent.ts:201`, `DialogueLogUI.ts:612-616` and `firstPersonDialogue.ts:115`. Confirm the metrics tests exercise mixed CJK and Latin text with `breakWords` and `letterSpacing` against real `pixi.js`.

**P3. Legacy blur used by the object-examine contact AO: no pixel coverage.** `contactAo.ts:308-321` uses `BlurFilter({ legacy: true, kernelSize: 9, quality: 2, resolution: 'inherit' })` on a half-resolution RenderTexture.
- The only blur parity case, `50_builtin_filters.ts:30-42`, is non-legacy with the default kernel size, on a resolution-1 target.
- `BlurFilter.test.ts` proves the WGSL is byte-identical to Pixi's **WebGPU** blur. Master ran Pixi's **WebGL** GLSL blur, so equivalence to master is unproven.
- **Task:** compare `blur/BlurFilterPass.ts` legacy passes (per-pass strength, `uStrength`, offsets per output frame) with the GLSL `generateBlurGlProgram` / `BlurFilterPass.mjs` GL path. Include kernel size 9 and a fractional target resolution.
- Also check `bgBlur` with strength 0 and quality 3 (`ObjectExamineScene.ts:1014`).

**P4. Gradient fills: game shape vs parity shape.** The game uses radial gradients with transparent colour stops and `textureSpace: 'local'` (`MenuUI.ts:1919`, `PanelSkin.ts:236`), and linear transparent-to-colour gradients (`UIDecor.ts:28,360`). The parity case is linear, opaque and in the default space (`60_graphics_text.ts:57`). `FillGradient.test.ts` compares only the generated gradient texture.
- **What to check:**
  - Is the gradient canvas uploaded premultiplied (the `uploadPremultiplied` path at `GpuTextures.ts:63-65`), matching Pixi WebGL?
  - Is the local texture-space matrix handled the same in batched and unbatched graphics? Unbatched starts at 200 or more vertices (`GraphicsContextSystem.ts:57`); a full-screen rectangle is batched.
  - Which gradient sampler style and address mode is used?

**P5. Unbatched graphics + texture fill + roundPixels.** `FrameBuilder.drawUnbatched` (`FrameBuilder.ts:613`) was only checked for blend mode. The game has 12 `Graphics.texture(...)` calls and large polylines and paths (121 `lineTo`, 14 `bezierCurveTo`), so it can cross the 400-float threshold.
- **Task:** compare against Pixi `GraphicsPipe.execute` / `GpuGraphicsAdaptor`: local uniform colour (tint × alpha), texture batch binding, and live reading of `roundPixels`.

**P6. Assets loader (not in any round-4 slice).** Files: `src/engine2d/assets/Assets.ts`, `loader/Loader.ts`, `loader/parsers/loadTextures.ts`, `cache/Cache.ts`, `resolver/*`.
- **Game users:** `UITextures.ts:38`, `HUD.ts:1154/1184`, `UIIcons.ts:37`, `MenuUI.ts:1628`, `InventoryUI.ts:890`, `CutsceneRenderer.ts:167` (relies on cache-key sharing and never unloads).
- **What to check:**
  - A failed load followed by a retry.
  - Concurrent loads of the same URL resolving to the same `Texture`.
  - Cache keys for relative vs absolute URLs, and URLs from `mediaUrlForRoot`.
  - `@2x` resolution parsing.
  - `Assets.unload` destroying textures still shared elsewhere.
  - `Texture.from(key)` lookup.

**P7. Resize + resolution + event mapping under the fixed-viewport letterbox.**
- `Renderer.setViewportSize` (`src/rendering/Renderer.ts:259-285`) calls `cancelResize`, sets `resizeTo = null`, calls `renderer.resize(w, h)`, then sets the canvas CSS to 100%. Unlike master, engine2d's `cancelResize` is a real function (`ResizePlugin.ts` header), and it runs with a queued requestAnimationFrame resize still pending.
- When `ResizePlugin.resize` calls `this.render()` synchronously, it goes through the game's crash-guard override.
- Check `EventSystem.mapPositionToPoint` (`EventSystem.ts:458-474`) with a CSS-scaled canvas at resolution 1.25 inside the letterbox. `rendererResize.test.ts` and `EventSystem.test.ts:174` cover the parts separately, but not this sequence end to end.

**P8. Interaction between a render exception and nested renders.**
- The game's crash guard (`Renderer.ts:120-140`) catches errors from `app.render`.
- `WebGPURenderer.render:258-267` aborts the builder and decrements the render depth.
- Check what happens when a throw comes from a nested RenderTexture render inside a ticker callback (lighting, contactAo, shadowPrefix) while an outer canvas frame is open inside `rhi.runFrame`: the RHI frame and pass state, the mask and stencil stacks in `stencilTargets`, and `gc.postrender` depth accounting.
- **How to test:** a NullRhi repro that throws from `onRender` at depth 2.

## Runtime-only checks (targeted tools/ab_compare or rhi_smoke runs)

- **R1. Resource growth.** Count RHI textures, buffers, pipelines and bind-group-cache entries across 10 scene round trips, and over 5 minutes of dialogue typewriter text. Compare the curve with master's GL object counts. The paths only a runtime run can prove are:
  - canvas text texture churn;
  - `Texture.from(canvas)` in `SceneLightingSystem`;
  - per-open RenderTextures in `contactAo`, `CharacterLightingSystem` and `irradianceProbe`;
  - the 1024-entry bind-group reset.
- **R2. First-use pipeline hitch.** `LumaRhiDevice.createRenderPipeline` (:1468) is synchronous, and prewarm covers only the VFX specs. Measure the frame-time spike when first entering a lit scene, the water minigame, burn, and object examine, against master's GL warm-up.
- **R3. Real WebGPU device loss during `readTexture` / `onSubmittedWorkDone`**, which r4-rhi left unverified. Add an rhi_smoke case.
- **R4. A pixel A/B at devicePixelRatio 1.25 and 1.5 of dialogue, inventory and menu screens.** This covers P2 and P4, since no parity tool renders the canvas root at a fractional resolution.
